name: Intravesical mitomycin (single instillation or induction)
cyclesNote: Two uses: (1) a single immediate post-TURBT instillation within 24 hours for low-risk NMIBC (cycles effectively 1), or (2) a 6-week induction course of weekly instillations for intermediate-risk disease (7-day cycle x 6). Gemcitabine is an accepted intravesical alternative agent.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Intravesical chemotherapy (mitomycin, or gemcitabine as an alternative) is used after complete TURBT to lower recurrence in low- and intermediate-risk NMIBC. No molecular biomarker gates its use.

supportiveCare: Do NOT give an immediate post-operative instillation if bladder perforation or extensive resection is suspected (risk of extravasation and severe reaction).
Retain in the bladder for about 1-2 hours, then void; alkalinization and reduced fluid intake before instillation improve mitomycin efficacy.
Manage chemical cystitis symptomatically; avoid skin/genital contact with voided drug.
monitoring: cystoscopy + cytology at first surveillance (about 3 months)

doseModificationRules.condition: significant chemical cystitis or suspected extravasation
doseModificationRules.text: Hold further instillations for severe cystitis; omit an immediate instillation entirely if perforation is suspected. Physician decides.

drugs.name: mitomycin
drugs.notes: mitomycin 40 mg instilled intravesically (reconstituted in about 20-40 mL sterile water or saline). Given as a single immediate post-TURBT dose (low-risk) or weekly x6 as induction (intermediate-risk). ISMP: 'mitomycin' is easily confused with mitoXANTRONE. Own wording; standard reference dose.

provenance.locator: Principles of Intravesical Therapy - intravesical chemotherapy (mitomycin)
